title: Kernel ensemble selector and warmup scheduler for stable FlashAttention v3 integration
creator: Ariana Patel
description: Design and implement an ensemble-based attention kernel selector and a coordinated warmup scheduler to improve stability and latency when integrating FlashAttention v3 across heterogeneous GPU fleets. Goal: reduce startup/regression incidents observed in v3 rollouts while recovering at least 95% of v2 tail latency for common workloads. The selector will score candidate kernels using a runtime fingerprint (sequence length distribution, dtype/quantization profile, batch shape), hardware characteristics, and recent telemetry. The warmup scheduler will orchestrate staged probing, reservoir-based sampling, and soft throttles to avoid workload-induced memory pressure during prefill/first-decode windows.
acceptance_criteria: Selector returns deterministic top-2 kernel candidates for 99.9% of production fingerprints during a 24h validation run
End-to-end median token latency degradation vs v2 <= 5% on representative customer traces
Tail (95th/99th) latency regressions reduced to prior baseline for >= 90% of test cases
Canary rollout automation: traffic ramp and automatic rollback on observed metric regressions
Integration tests and perf harnesses added to CI with synthetic and recorded workloads
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring functions and kernel compatibility matrix (CPU/GPU/quantization variants)
Integration perf runs: short, medium, long context traces with diverse batch shapes and quant profiles
Canary in staging with 5% traffic, collect token-level latency, memory headroom, and error rates for 48h
Chaos test: simulate memory pressure + high concurrency and ensure warmup scheduler backoffs within configured SLOs
A/B comparison against existing heuristic selector used in runtime-1.20 with identical workload replay
observability: New metrics: selector_choice (enum), selector_score_{kernel}, warmup_phase, warmup_backoff_count
Tagging: attach fingerprint and kernel metadata to existing token traces in tracer
Dashboards: add runtime-attn/kernel-ensemble (Grafana) and alert thresholds for tail latency delta > 10%
Logs: structured entry for kernel handoff events including memory footprint and chosen workspace layout
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal staging run (traffic=100% internal) for 72h
Stage 2: canary in us-west-2 (traffic=5%) for 48h with auto-rolloff on alert
Stage 3: incremental ramp to 25% then 50% with monitoring windows and manual check-ins
Fallback: immediate deterministic fallback to v2/compatible kernel via existing policy if memory headroom < 10% or 5xx spikes
notes: Motivation: multiple customers observed intermittent 99th-percentile spikes when v3 kernels were selected on cold prefills. Root cause correlated to aggressive workspace layouts + kernel warmup that forced eviction patterns on multi-tenant nodes.

Approach: use ensemble scoring combining (a) microbenchmarks collected on node start, (b) historical latency traces for fingerprint, and (c) a stability score derived from recent error/oom events. Weighted scoring allows bias toward stable v2-equivalent kernels when confidence is low.
Trade-offs: ensemble selector adds ~150us decision overhead per prefill in the worst case; mitigated by caching decisions per fingerprint and hierarchical evaluation (cheap heuristics first).

Performance: preliminary staging perf runs show median token latency improvement of 3-7% vs naive v3 rollout on conversational traces and 10-12% cost reduction on long-context batched workloads due to better kernel packing. Tail improvements vary by workload but preliminary SLO recovery observed in 80% of cases.

Open questions: best decay policy for cached decisions (time vs opaques seen), how to incorporate quantization-aware microbenchmarks without inflating probe budget, safe memory thresholds across instance types.
